title: "Stage 6 – Reading the curve you joined"
aliases:
  - /tracks/self-study/stage-6.html
---
This stage asks what the curve you joined establishes, now that your own dot is on it. Both pages are short, and both are more useful after Task 5 than before it.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd) | Where the idea came from, the three purposes that a multiverse can serve and why they pull apart, and the critical positions of 2025–26 read against the curve of the claim. | 60 minutes |
| [The multiverse: the one-correct-analysis position](../../companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-lakens) | Sections 4 and 9.2 deserve their own sitting. Grant the argument for a moment and ask what would follow for the specification that you preregistered in Task 5. | 30 minutes |
| [Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) | Why 864 estimates are not 864 independent tests, what a permutation design would supply, and what stands without one. | 45 minutes |

**By the end of the stage** you can say what the curve you joined establishes about the claim, what it does not, and what would have to be run for it to establish more.
